title: You’re Good!
transcript: Today's day 15 of reviewing my followers games until I hit 100,000 followers. Today is the turn of the greater Kami who writes, "I do follow all the basics but still not going up." If you want to be next, all you have to do is follow me, like this video, and comment your chess.com username. So, Kami, this is the last game you lost in your profile. You decided to play a Caro-Kann Defense and I have to say you played the opening pretty much perfectly. So, this suggests that you have studied your opening and you have already equalized the position from the opening. After a few more moves, you continue to improve your position. I like how you reroute the pieces, you castle, and you're actually slightly better. But here is where it starts to go a little bit south. You create this battery with the queen and bishop threatening checkmate, which is all good. You are better in this position. But now that your queen and bishop are in this position, you need to be aware of the pattern of knight b5 in this case that attacks both of them and is going to win your bishop for a knight. Instead, you decide to move your king away like this and this doesn't really make any sense to me. I suppose that you were trying to get out of this pin, but there are other ways to solve this position. For example, f5 counter-attacking the queen. And if the queen moves away, for example, here, now you can jump in with the knight and you are threatening a fork of the queen and king. Something like that would have kept more tension and kept the initiative for you. Whereas after you just move your king and knight b5 is played, you're going to lose all of your steam. The bishop was one of the key pieces in your position and now this is back to equality. So, after a few more moves, you break in the center. I don't mind this. You reroute your queen, but then you decide to bite more than you can chew because in this position, unfortunately, we blundered the move b5. This is simply going to win material because the queen is looking at the rook and now the rook is looking at the rook. So, if you move the knight like you did in the game, you're going to get checkmated. But if you don't, you're just going to lose the knight. So, I think you're right. You're following the principles pretty well, but you are lacking a little bit is pattern recognition. And you need to be more mindful of the tension between the pieces. We should have registered the pressure of the queen on this rook. We should have registered the fact that after we take here and the rook comes to this file, now the rook is x-raying all of the pieces on this file including the rook. And we need to keep in mind the fact that there is the threat of attacking the knight with the pawn. You played this entire sequence in under 10 seconds. You have 8 minutes and a half. We cannot afford to be spending only a couple of seconds for these moves, especially when there is this much tension and it is so crucial to find the right plan. So I think that at this stage you need to work on your time usage and pattern recognition because you quite clearly have a decent understanding of the game, but you are making more concrete mistakes like missing B5 here and knight B5 here.
